text:
Jordan (support): Hey team — customer Jane reports 500 + spikey latency on POST /v1/generate. She gave a request_id: abc123-7f4e. Can we locate server-side logs for that req? They said event happened ~2026-03-15T14:22:10Z.

customer_jane: Repro curl I used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": "summarize: ..."}' \
  -H 'X-Request-Id: abc123-7f4e'
```

Jordan (support): Thanks — can someone run a KQL/ES needle for that request_id? Also, retention question: customer is on free tier, wondering if logs may have aged out.

Priya (sre): Looking. Quick note: hot index TTL is 72h by default for non-enterprise customers, then archived to cold storage for 90d. If this is >72h old we may need to pull from archive snapshot.

Priya (sre): KQL I ran (narrow):
```kql
service:edge AND request_id:"abc123-7f4e" OR trace.request_id:"abc123-7f4e" | sort by @timestamp desc | limit 200
```

Priya (sre): Result: a handful of edge logs at 2026-03-15T14:22:10.523 showing upstream reset and then 502 from runtime pool. No detailed runtime stack in hot index — likely rotated. I can export archive but need approval from eng for debug bundle retrieval. :mag_right:

Liam (eng): Confirmed — runtime nodes wrote error: 
```
E 14:22:11.587 runtime/serve.go:413 request abc123-7f4e failed: kvcache miss + kernel_timeout
```
But full trace lived in node-local logs that were shipped to cold after rotation. I can pull an archive if we have customer consent for debug bundle.

customer_jane: Yes please — you have my consent. Also want repro steps so my team can avoid this.

Jordan (support): Ok, two parallel actions: 1) Priya, can you attach the small hot-index snippet to this thread; 2) Liam, please request the archive pull and generate a debug bundle.

Priya (sre): Pasted 3 hot-index lines below (redacted tokens):
```
2026-03-15T14:22:10.523 edge - req=abc123-7f4e client=10.1.2.3 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=502 upstream=127.0.0.1:8080 proto=http/1.1
2026-03-15T14:22:10.530 edge - req=abc123-7f4e trace_id=trc-55aa level=info msg="forwarding to runtime" shard=us-west-2
2026-03-15T14:22:11.587 edge - req=abc123-7f4e level=error msg="upstream reset" code=ECONNRESET
```

Priya (sre): If you need to run this yourself, use this KQL endpoint example (replace index and timewindow):
```bash
# Kibana curl example (support-only):
curl -s -H "Authorization: ApiKey $ES_APIKEY" \
  "https://es.internal.redwood/_search" -d '{"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"match": {"request_id":"abc123-7f4e"}}]}}}'
```

Liam (eng): Archive pull queued (ticket: ARCH-4621). ETA ~45m. When archive is ready I'll create a debug bundle and attach a presigned link. Debug bundle command I use internally: `rw-debug bundle --req abc123-7f4e --include=node-logs,kvcache,dump` and it uploads to s3 with restricted ACL.

logbot: Archive job ARCH-4621 started by Liam (eng) at 2026-03-17T02:10:01Z.

Jordan (support): Great — customer, in the meantime can you try adding the header `X-Client-Timeout: 30s` and re-run the curl once to see if you can hit a different backend? This helps surface whether it's a transient kernel timeout vs sustained capacity issue.

customer_jane: Will do and report back. Also, is there a quick way to produce a debug bundle from our side? We're on a shared hosting setup.

Liam (eng): For customers we provide a trimmed debug bundle helper:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debugbundle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"request_id":"abc123-7f4e","include": ["edge-logs","headers"]}'
```
This will produce a small bundle (no node-local logs) that helps correlate headers and edge events. For the full runtime traces we need the archive pull which support/eng already started.

Priya (sre): FYI retention/lookup TL;DR: hot index (72h) -> cold archive (90d) -> longterm snapshot (>90d needs legal/enterprise export). So always try hot KQL first; if not found escalate with ARCH ticket.

Jordan (support): I'll keep this thread updated. Once Liam attaches the presigned bundle link I'll post it and mark this escalated. :thumbsup:

customer_jane: Thanks everyone. I'll try the X-Client-Timeout tweak and post results here.

Liam (eng): Archive available: https://s3.redwood.internal/arch/ARCH-4621/abc123-7f4e-debug.tar.gz (internal access only). Created debug bundle and added stack trace snippets to ticket.

Jordan (support): Attached archive link to support ticket and asked for redaction steps. Closing loop when customer confirms repro.

customer_jane: Confirmed — adding X-Client-Timeout fixed the immediate 500s; looks like transient kernel timeout. Please confirm best practice to avoid (client-side retry/backoff or different batch config).

Liam (eng): We'll follow up on recommended client-side retries + server-side batching cap tweaks. I'll open a follow-up RFC with suggested batch/window defaults for public docs.

Jordan (support): Marking resolved for now, re-open if anything else shows up. :white_check_mark:
